routing.reason: Input validation and error handling in a ~340-line app (src/app.ts, public/app.js, tests), with fully specified, testable acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: workflow default — a bug without urgency, the normal plan and review path fits — cost if wrong: an extra plan gate for a small fix
Ruling: skip prd, architecture, ux, seo — small bug with no design, no cross-cutting decision, no public page change — cost if wrong: none notable
Ruling: keep frame (po) at low effort — the ticket's criteria are already testable, so the PO only needs to check side effects such as PATCH and the page's error display — cost if wrong: a few cents
Ruling: security effort medium — request parsing and error disclosure change, but there is no auth, payment or personal data — cost if wrong: a missed hardening note
Ruling: budget $1.50 — size S covering the plan, one task, one or two review rounds and the security review — cost if wrong: the run stops before its reviews and needs more budget

first: test/tasks.test.ts(168,106): error TS7006: Parameter 't' implicitly has an 'any' type.

criteria.why: validateTitle rejects missing, empty, blank and non-string titles with 400 'title is required' before createTask; tests cover each case and check nothing is created.
PATCH validates when 'title' in body, using the same rule; tests cover empty, blank, numeric and null titles and an unchanged task.
Length is checked after trim with the exact message, and the trimmed title is saved; tests cover 201 characters, exactly 200, and padded titles.
readJson turns a JSON.parse failure into HttpError(400, 'invalid JSON body'); tested on POST and PATCH.
The catch handler logs with console.error and sends 500 'internal error'; a test breaks the DB and checks the response and the log call.
The submit handler wraps the call in try/catch and calls show(err), which presumably displays err.message from the API error. The diff doesn't show the api() and show() helpers, so this is assumed.
Tests cover the validation, trimming, invalid JSON and 500 cases. The page change (criterion 6) has no test.

findings.what: readJson silently turns a valid non-object JSON body (null, array, number) into {}. On PATCH this means such a body is accepted as a no-op, and the response isn't a 400. The ticket doesn't ask for 400 here, so this is a judgment call.
The `"title" in body` check on PATCH is correct. `done` is still passed through unvalidated, which is outside the ticket.
The UI error display (criterion 6) has no test. It depends on the show() and api() helpers, which aren't in the diff.
HttpError is declared after its use in readJson. This works because classes are only used at call time, but it reads slightly out of order.
The 500 test builds a temp file DB and drops the table from a second connection. It is somewhat elaborate, but it exercises the real path.

judge.summary: The diff meets every criterion: shared title validation on POST and PATCH, a clean HttpError path, a generic logged 500, and a UI try/catch. The tests are thorough, including the trim boundary and the no-leak 500. The remaining gaps are minor: non-object JSON bodies are quietly treated as empty, and the UI change has no test.
